stem: The student wants to describe the method of Okafor's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A muscle's temperature affects how quickly its fibers can contract.
• Sports scientist Leilani Okafor asked whether heated jackets could preserve sprint speed during the wait between a warm-up and a race.
• She had 18 sprinters rest for 20 minutes after warming up, wearing either battery-heated jackets or standard tracksuits, and then timed their 30-meter sprints.
• Sprinters in heated jackets ran an average of 0.06 seconds faster.
• Okafor concluded that passive heating can offset some of the benefit lost while athletes wait.
choices: Okafor's study found that sprinters who wore heated jackets while waiting ran 30 meters an average of 0.06 seconds faster.
To test heated jackets, Okafor timed 30-meter sprints by 18 athletes who had rested for 20 minutes in either heated jackets or tracksuits.
Okafor wanted to learn whether heated jackets could preserve an athlete's sprint speed between the warm-up and the race.
Since muscle temperature affects contraction speed, Okafor concluded that passive heating can offset some lost warm-up benefit.
explanation: The goal asks for the study's method, meaning what Okafor actually did. Choice B's main clause gives exactly that: she timed 30-meter sprints by 18 athletes after a 20-minute rest in one of two kinds of clothing. The other choices each describe a different stage of the study.

A.why: You picked a sentence about the right study but the wrong stage. It reports the result, the 0.06-second gain, and not how the study was carried out.

C.why: This gives Okafor's research question, which is the aim, not the method. You matched the study's name without checking which stage the goal asked for.

D.why: This combines the background note with Okafor's conclusion. It is accurate, but it tells you what she decided and says nothing about how she tested it.

stem: The student wants to specify how long the Corvell dune beetle remains in its larval stage. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Corvell dune beetle lives in coastal dunes along the southern shore of Lake Arvana.
• The species is named for Harold Corvell, a park ranger who collected the first specimen in 1987.
• Adults are active only at night, when sand temperatures drop below 25°C.
• Its larvae feed on the roots of beach grass, a plant that holds the dunes in place.
• Larvae continue feeding for up to three years before they pupate.
choices: The Corvell dune beetle is named for Harold Corvell, the park ranger who collected the species' first specimen.
Adult Corvell dune beetles are active only at night, when the temperature of the sand drops below 25°C.
Corvell dune beetle larvae feed on the roots of beach grass, a plant that holds the lakeshore dunes in place.
Corvell dune beetle larvae spend up to three years feeding on beach grass roots before they pupate.
explanation: The goal ends with a specific question: how long the beetle remains a larva. Only one note answers it, the one saying larvae feed for up to three years before pupating. Choice D is built around that duration.

A.why: You were drawn in by the beetle's name. This explains where the name came from, not how long the larval stage lasts.

B.why: This describes adults, a different life stage, and gives a temperature rather than a length of time.

C.why: This is the closest miss. It is about larvae, but it tells you what they eat, not how long they stay larvae. Check that the choice answers the exact question the goal ends with.

stem: The student wants to describe what distinguishes the Belen variety from standard sorghum. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2019, the Lindqvist Crop Institute released three new sorghum varieties: Amara, Belen, and Sotto.
• All three were bred for farms in semiarid regions of East Africa.
• Amara matures in 95 days, about two weeks sooner than traditional varieties.
• Belen produces grain with 20 percent more iron than standard sorghum.
• Sotto has stiff stalks that resist bending in strong winds.
choices: Belen, one of three sorghum varieties released in 2019, was bred for farms in semiarid regions of East Africa.
The three sorghum varieties released in 2019, Amara, Belen, and Sotto, were each bred for semiarid East African farms.
The grain of Belen, a sorghum variety released in 2019, contains 20 percent more iron than that of standard sorghum.
Unlike Belen, the Amara variety matures in 95 days, about two weeks sooner than traditional sorghum varieties.
explanation: The goal names one variety, Belen, and one restriction: what sets it apart from standard sorghum. In Choice C, Belen's grain is the subject of the sentence, and the main clause gives its distinguishing trait, 20 percent more iron than standard sorghum.

A.why: This names Belen but describes something all three varieties share. A trait shared across the group cannot be what distinguishes Belen.

B.why: This describes the whole set of varieties when the goal asks about one of them. It never says anything specific to Belen.

D.why: This is mainly about Amara, and 'Unlike Belen' implies Belen does not mature early, which the notes never say. You let Belen's name appear in the sentence without checking whether Belen is actually the subject.

stem: The student wants to describe how dyed wool is used in the Harvest Star coverlet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ingrid Halvorsen (1841–1919) was a Norwegian-born weaver who settled in Wisconsin in 1868.
• She is known for jacquard coverlets woven for local families.
• Her 1874 coverlet Harvest Star combines undyed linen with wool.
• In Harvest Star, she used madder-dyed wool only for the eight-pointed stars at the center of each block.
• Her coverlets from the 1890s used commercially dyed aniline yarns throughout.
choices: Halvorsen's Harvest Star coverlet reserves madder-dyed wool for the eight-pointed stars at the center of each block.
Harvest Star was woven in 1874 by Halvorsen, a Norwegian-born weaver who had settled in Wisconsin six years earlier.
In her coverlets from the 1890s, Halvorsen used yarns that had been commercially dyed with aniline throughout.
Halvorsen's Harvest Star coverlet, like all of her other jacquard coverlets, combines undyed linen with wool.
explanation: The goal names one work, Harvest Star, and one feature, how dyed wool is used in it. Choice A's main clause gives that detail directly: madder-dyed wool appears only in the central eight-pointed stars.

B.why: This names Harvest Star but spends the sentence on the weaver's biography. You matched the title and missed that the goal asks about the coverlet's materials.

C.why: This is about dyed yarn, but in Halvorsen's 1890s coverlets, not Harvest Star. You matched the topic and missed the restriction to a single work.

D.why: The notes never say that all of her coverlets used linen and wool, and the 1890s aniline yarns suggest they didn't. This choice also describes undyed linen, not how dyed wool is used.

stem: The student wants to indicate how old the Pallidophyllum fossils are. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Pallidophyllum is an extinct genus of flowering plant known only from fossil leaves.
• The first Pallidophyllum fossils were found in 1954 in shale near Ashgrove, Montana.
• In 2022, paleobotanist Tomás Ferreira-Ng identified microscopic pores on the undersides of the leaves.
• The density of these pores suggests that the plant grew when atmospheric carbon dioxide levels were high.
• Radiometric dating of volcanic ash above the shale shows that the leaves are at least 94 million years old.
choices: The first Pallidophyllum fossils, leaves preserved in shale near Ashgrove, Montana, were discovered in 1954.
Radiometric dating of volcanic ash above the shale shows that Pallidophyllum leaves are precisely 94 million years old.
Radiometric dating of volcanic ash above the shale shows that Pallidophyllum leaves are at least 94 million years old.
The density of pores on Pallidophyllum leaves suggests that the plant grew when carbon dioxide levels were high.
explanation: The goal asks for the fossils' age, and exactly one note gives it. Choice C reports that age accurately, including the qualifier 'at least,' which matters because ash lying above the shale can only set a minimum age.

A.why: You saw a date and took it for an age. 1954 is when the fossils were discovered, which says nothing about how old they are.

B.why: This uses the right note but changes 'at least' to 'precisely.' The dating gives only a minimum age, so you treated a lower bound as an exact figure.

D.why: This describes the conditions the plant grew in, which hints at a period of time but never states how old the fossils are.
